text: Caldwell Logistics runs a single on-premises Active Directory forest, caldwell.local, with roughly six hundred employees across three regional offices. Moving email and file storage to Microsoft 365 means every one of those on-prem accounts needs a matching identity in Microsoft Entra ID — and this lesson walks through exactly how that sync gets set up, verified, and connected to the Conditional Access policy built back in Chapter 2.

The Entra Connect installer runs on a member server, never a domain controller. Caldwell's team chooses Custom installation instead of Express, because Express would sync every OU with password hash sync and no filtering at all. Caldwell only wants its three active OUs in scope for this phase, holding back a legacy OU still full of stale service accounts. The wizard walks through selecting Password Hash Sync as the sign-in method and picking those three OUs before running its first full sync.

Federation was on the table, but it would mean standing up and maintaining an ADFS farm — a second set of servers, a certificate renewal cycle, and a new piece of on-prem infrastructure that becomes a single point of failure for every cloud sign-in if it goes down. Caldwell's infrastructure team is two people. Password hash sync keeps the actual authentication decision inside Entra ID itself, which means Conditional Access and Identity Protection's risk-based sign-in work natively, with nothing extra to configure or keep patched on-prem.

Finishing the wizard isn't the same as confirming it worked. Get-ADSyncScheduler shows the sync interval — thirty minutes by default — and Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta forces an immediate sync instead of waiting on it. Get-ADSyncConnectorRunStatus surfaces any connector-space errors, like the duplicate-attribute conflicts that are the most common reason a single user silently fails to sync.

Sync completing isn't the finish line either. In the Entra admin center, a synced user's profile shows Directory synced: Yes and a source of Windows Server AD. More important: pulling up that user's sign-in logs and checking the Conditional Access tab should show the Chapter 2 MFA policy as Success, not Not applied. And if that policy targets a synced security group rather than all users, the group's own membership has to have synced too, or the policy simply never sees those accounts.

That's hybrid identity actually working end to end — not just installed, but verified and connected to the policy that depends on it. Next up: Lesson 30 takes Caldwell's data through encryption at rest with a customer-managed key, and moves an application's hardcoded database connection string into Key Vault with rotation in place.
